dropped.reason: Grignard reaction of aldehydes (CH3MgBr) is not in the 2017 Stage 6 syllabus

questions.question: The graph shows the variation in $\Delta G$ with temperature ($T$) for a reaction. Which of the following statements is true?
questions.answer: A reaction is spontaneous (feasible) when $\Delta G<0$. The line crosses $\Delta G=0$ at 300 K and is negative at higher temperatures, so the reaction is feasible above 300 K (C).
options: The reaction is feasible above 300 K.
The reaction is feasible below 300 K.

questions.question: In which ONE of the following reactions at equilibrium will the YIELD of the product increase when the VOLUME of the container is increased at constant temperature?
questions.answer: Increasing the volume lowers the pressure, so the equilibrium shifts towards the side with more moles of gas. Only the reaction in A has more moles of gas on the product side (1 mol → 2 mol), so its yield increases (A). B has equal moles on each side; C and D have fewer moles of gas on the product side.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the use of the equilibrium constant in relation to the solubility of ionic substances? The equilibrium constant:
questions.answer: The solubility product constant $K_{sp}$ describes the equilibrium between a slightly soluble ionic solid and its ions in solution, and can be used to calculate how much dissolves (molar solubility) (B).
options: can only be determined for soluble substances.
can be used to determine the solubility of ionic substances.
does not give any useful information about the solubility of ionic substances.
cannot be used for partially soluble substances, as they are not a homogenous system.

questions.question: Equal moles of nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$, reddish brown) and dinitrogen tetroxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, colourless) are sealed inside Chamber 1 of a two-chamber reactor at $25^\circ$C. After a while the equilibrium $2\text{NO}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$, $\Delta H^\circ=-58\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ is established inside Chamber 1. More $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$ is added to Chamber 1. What observations would be made about the colour of the gas mixture and its temperature after a new equilibrium is established?
questions.answer: Adding $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ shifts the equilibrium to the left (reverse), producing more reddish brown $\text{NO}_2$, so the mixture becomes darker brown. The reverse reaction is endothermic (the forward reaction has $\Delta H<0$), so it absorbs heat and the temperature decreases (B).

questions.question: This follows on from Question 4. The valve between the chambers is opened, allowing the gas mixture in Chamber 1 to fill both chambers. Which statement describes the initial and final observations of the gas mixture's colour in Chamber 1 as a new equilibrium is established?
questions.answer:
When the gas expands into both chambers the concentrations of all gases fall immediately, so the mixture initially looks paler brown. The pressure has decreased, so the equilibrium $2\text{NO}_2\rightleftharpoons\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ shifts towards the side with more moles of gas (the $\text{NO}_2$ side). More $\text{NO}_2$ forms, so the mixture becomes darker again (A).
*(The school's explanation says the system shifts to the side with fewer moles, which contradicts its own key; the correct shift for a pressure decrease is towards more moles of gas.)*
options: Initially paler brown; became even paler
Initially darker brown; became even darker

questions.question: Photosynthesis occurs in plants: $6\text{CO}_2(g)+6\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\rightarrow\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6(aq)+6\text{O}_2(g)$ (chlorophyll, sunlight). Which row of the table correctly identifies the links between changes in entropy and enthalpy for combustion reactions and photosynthesis?
questions.answer: Photosynthesis forms fewer, more ordered molecules (12 gas molecules → 6 gas molecules plus a dissolved solid), so entropy decreases, and it needs a continuous input of energy (endothermic). Combustion produces more gas molecules (entropy increases) and releases energy (exothermic) (C).
options: Entropy: photosynthesis decreases, combustion increases; Enthalpy: photosynthesis exothermic, combustion endothermic
Entropy: photosynthesis increases, combustion decreases; Enthalpy: photosynthesis endothermic, combustion exothermic
Entropy: photosynthesis decreases, combustion increases; Enthalpy: photosynthesis endothermic, combustion exothermic
Entropy: photosynthesis increases, combustion decreases; Enthalpy: photosynthesis exothermic, combustion endothermic

questions.question: Which alternative most correctly represents the equilibrium expression for the reaction $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3(s)+3\text{CO}(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{Fe}(s)+3\text{CO}_2(g)$?
questions.answer: Pure solids are not included in the equilibrium expression, so $K_{eq}=\dfrac{[\text{CO}_2]^3}{[\text{CO}]^3}$ (A).

questions.question: $50.00$ mL of a $0.020$ M solution of $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is added to $50.00$ mL of a $0.060$ M solution of $\text{HNO}_3$. The hydrogen ion concentration in the resultant solution, in mol L$^{-1}$, is
questions.answer: $n(\text{H}^+)=0.060\times0.05000=3.0\times10^{-3}$ mol. $n(\text{OH}^-)=2\times0.020\times0.05000=2.0\times10^{-3}$ mol. After neutralisation, $n(\text{H}^+)=1.0\times10^{-3}$ mol in $0.100$ L: $[\text{H}^+]=0.010$ mol L$^{-1}$ (A).

questions.question: Use the following acid ionisation constants to identify the correct decreasing order of base strengths: HF, $K_a=7.2\times10^{-4}$; $\text{HNO}_2$, $K_a=4.5\times10^{-4}$; HCN, $K_a=6.2\times10^{-10}$.
questions.answer: The weaker the acid, the stronger its conjugate base ($K_b=K_w/K_a$). HCN is the weakest acid, then $\text{HNO}_2$, then HF, so the base strengths decrease in the order $\text{CN}^->\text{NO}_2^->\text{F}^-$ ($K_b$: $1.6\times10^{-5}>2.2\times10^{-11}>1.4\times10^{-11}$) (A).

questions.question: Which statement best represents Davy's definition of an acid?
questions.answer: Davy showed that hydrochloric acid contains no oxygen (disproving Lavoisier's theory) and proposed that the presence of hydrogen, which can be replaced by a metal, gives acids their properties (C). Proton donors is the Brønsted–Lowry definition and ionisation is Arrhenius's.
options: Acids ionise in solution to form hydrogen ions.

questions.question: $\text{NaOCl}$ is completely dissociated in water to form $\text{Na}^+(aq)$ and $\text{OCl}^-(aq)$. In solution, $\text{OCl}^-$ hydrolyses according to $\text{OCl}^-(aq)+\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\rightleftharpoons\text{HOCl}(aq)+\text{OH}^-(aq)$. $1.0$ L of pure water at constant temperature is added to a $1.0$ L solution of $0.10$ M NaOCl. When the solution reaches equilibrium again, the:
questions.answer: Dilution lowers all concentrations; the equilibrium shifts towards the side with more dissolved particles, but $[\text{OH}^-]$ still ends up lower than before (the solution is less basic), so $[\text{H}^+]$ has increased and the pH has decreased (B). $[\text{HOCl}]$ is lower than initially, and the equilibrium constant depends only on temperature, which is unchanged.
options: pH of the solution has decreased.
value of the equilibrium constant has halved.

questions.question: One litre of an aqueous solution of potassium hydroxide (KOH) has a pH of 12.0 at $25^\circ$C. The amount of solid KOH, in mol, that must be added to the solution to raise the pH to 13.0 would be:

One litre of an aqueous solution of potassium hydroxide has a pH of 12.0 at $25^\circ$C. The amount of pure HCl gas, in mol, that must be added to the solution to lower the pH from 12.0 to 2.0 would be:
questions.answer: The initial $0.01$ mol of $\text{OH}^-$ must be neutralised by $0.01$ mol HCl, and a further $0.01$ mol HCl is then needed to give $[\text{H}^+]=10^{-2}=0.01$ M: total $0.02$ mol (C).

questions.question: Potassium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid react in aqueous solution: $\text{KOH}(aq)+\text{HCl}(aq)\rightarrow\text{KCl}(aq)+\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. A $50$ mL solution containing $0.025$ mol of KOH was mixed rapidly in an insulated vessel with a $50$ mL solution containing $0.025$ mol of HCl. The temperature increased by $3.5^\circ$C. Assuming that the specific heat capacity of the solution is the same as that of water, the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, of this reaction, in kJ mol$^{-1}$, is closest to:
questions.answer: $q=mc\Delta T=100\times4.18\times3.5=1463\ \text{J}=1.463$ kJ. $\Delta H=-\dfrac qn=-\dfrac{1.463}{0.025}=-58.5\approx-59$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (B).

questions.question: Which of the following diagrams shows the apparatus correctly set up for heating under reflux?
questions.answer: Reflux uses a vertical condenser above the flask so that vapours condense and return to the flask. A and B show distillation set-ups (sloping condenser, collection flask). In D the water enters at the top and leaves at the bottom, which is incorrect; cooling water must enter at the bottom and leave at the top so the jacket stays full. C is correct (C).

questions.question: When but-1-ene reacts with hydrogen chloride, 1-chlorobutane and 2-chlorobutane are formed. According to Markovnikov's rule:
questions.answer: Markovnikov's rule: the hydrogen adds to the carbon of the double bond that already has more hydrogens (C1), so the chlorine adds to C2. The major product is 2-chlorobutane (B).
options: There will be equal proportions of both products.
It is impossible to tell the relative proportions of each product.

questions.question: Consider the following chemical compounds (1: 2-chloropropane, 2: propan-2-ol, 3: propene). Which of the following correctly identifies X, Y and Z in the reaction sequence X →(dehydration) Y →(addition) Z?
questions.answer: Dehydration removes water from an alcohol to form an alkene, so X is the alcohol (2) and Y the alkene (3). Addition of HCl to the alkene gives the haloalkane Z (1): 2, 3, 1 (D).

questions.question: The structure shows propanoic acid. Which of the following shows the splitting pattern for the circled H atom (on the $\text{CH}_2$ carbon), in a high resolution proton NMR spectrum?
questions.answer: The circled H is on the $\text{CH}_2$ carbon, whose neighbouring carbon ($\text{CH}_3$) has 3 hydrogens. By the $n+1$ rule the signal is split into $3+1=4$ peaks, a quartet (1:3:3:1) (C).

questions.question: A simplified mass spectrum of an organic compound is shown (peaks at m/z 15, 59 and 74). Which of the following compounds could NOT have produced the spectrum?
questions.answer: The peak at m/z 74 is the molecular ion, so the compound has $M_r=74$. Options A, B and D are $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ (74.08), $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ and $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ (74.12) respectively. Option C, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N}$, has $M_r=73.14$, so it could not give a molecular ion at 74 (C).

questions.question: Construct an equation for the equilibrium that occurs in a saturated solution of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$.
questions.answer: $\text{Mg(OH)}_2(s)\rightleftharpoons\text{Mg}^{2+}(aq)+2\text{OH}^-(aq)$

questions.question: Construct an expression for the $K_{sp}$ of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$.
questions.answer: $K_{sp}=[\text{Mg}^{2+}][\text{OH}^-]^2$ (the solid is not included).

questions.question: Calculate the molar solubility of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ in water at $25^\circ$C, and give $[\text{Mg}^{2+}]$ and $[\text{OH}^-]$. Use the solubility constant given on the data sheet ($K_{sp}=5.61\times10^{-12}$).
questions.answer:
Let the molar solubility be $s$: $[\text{Mg}^{2+}]=s$, $[\text{OH}^-]=2s$.
$$K_{sp}=s(2s)^2=4s^3=5.61\times10^{-12}\Rightarrow s=\sqrt[3]{\frac{5.61\times10^{-12}}{4}}=1.12\times10^{-4}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$$
*(The school's sample answer gives $1.19\times10^{-4}$; the cube root of $1.4025\times10^{-12}$ is $1.12\times10^{-4}$.)* So:
- molar solubility of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2=1.12\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$
- $[\text{Mg}^{2+}]=1.12\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$
- $[\text{OH}^-]=2.24\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$

questions.question: When dilute sodium hydroxide, NaOH, is added to a saturated solution of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, the concentration of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions in the saturated solution decreases. Explain why.
questions.answer: NaOH dissociates completely, adding $\text{OH}^-$ ions, which are common to the equilibrium $\text{Mg(OH)}_2(s)\rightleftharpoons\text{Mg}^{2+}(aq)+2\text{OH}^-(aq)$ (the common ion effect). The increase in $[\text{OH}^-]$ disturbs the equilibrium, and by Le Chatelier's principle the system shifts to oppose the change, in the direction that removes $\text{OH}^-$: to the left. $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions combine with $\text{OH}^-$ to form more solid $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ (precipitate), so $[\text{Mg}^{2+}]$ decreases. (The ion product $[\text{Mg}^{2+}][\text{OH}^-]^2$ exceeds $K_{sp}$ until enough solid has precipitated to restore it.)

questions.question: Calculate the concentration of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions in a solution after $30.0$ mL of $0.120$ mol L$^{-1}$ NaOH is added to $20.0$ mL of a saturated $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ solution. State any assumptions that have been made.
questions.answer:
$n(\text{OH}^-)$ added $=0.120\times0.0300=3.60\times10^{-3}$ mol, in a total volume of $50.0$ mL: $[\text{OH}^-]=\dfrac{3.60\times10^{-3}}{0.0500}=0.0720$ M.

At the new equilibrium $K_{sp}=[\text{Mg}^{2+}][\text{OH}^-]^2$ (the large $[\text{OH}^-]$ forces the $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ to precipitate until the ion product again equals $K_{sp}$):
$$[\text{Mg}^{2+}]=\frac{K_{sp}}{[\text{OH}^-]^2}=\frac{5.61\times10^{-12}}{(0.0720)^2}=1.08\times10^{-9}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$$
**Assumptions:** the volumes are additive (50.0 mL); the $\text{OH}^-$ from the dissolved $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ and the $\text{OH}^-$ used in precipitating $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ are negligible compared with the $0.0720$ M added, so $[\text{OH}^-]\approx0.0720$ M; the temperature remains $25^\circ$C so $K_{sp}$ is unchanged.

questions.question: Boron trichloride ($\text{BCl}_3$) is a gas that reacts with hydrogen gas to produce solid boron and hydrogen chloride gas. Construct a balanced equation for this reaction.
questions.answer: $2\text{BCl}_3(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightarrow2\text{B}(s)+6\text{HCl}(g)$

questions.question: The reaction is endothermic with $\Delta H^\circ=+127\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The standard entropy change is $\Delta S^\circ=79.4\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$. Calculate $\Delta G^\circ$ for this reaction at 298 K. State if the reaction is spontaneous at this temperature.
questions.answer:
$$\Delta G^\circ=\Delta H^\circ-T\Delta S^\circ=127-(298)(0.0794)=127-23.7=103\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$
(entropy converted to kJ K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$). Since $\Delta G^\circ>0$, the reaction is not spontaneous at 298 K.

questions.question: A $1.00$ L vessel contains, at equilibrium, $0.300$ mol of $\text{N}_2$, $0.400$ mol $\text{H}_2$ and $0.100$ mol $\text{NH}_3$: $\text{N}_2(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NH}_3(g)$. If the temperature of the vessel is kept constant, how many moles of $\text{H}_2(g)$ must be introduced into the vessel in order to double the equilibrium concentration of $\text{NH}_3(g)$?
questions.answer:
Initial equilibrium: $K_{eq}=\dfrac{[\text{NH}_3]^2}{[\text{N}_2][\text{H}_2]^3}=\dfrac{(0.100)^2}{(0.300)(0.400)^3}=0.521$.

Let $s$ mol of $\text{H}_2$ be added. To double $[\text{NH}_3]$ to $0.200$ M, $0.100$ mol $\text{NH}_3$ must form, which uses $0.050$ mol $\text{N}_2$ and $0.150$ mol $\text{H}_2$:

| | $\text{N}_2$ | $\text{H}_2$ | $\text{NH}_3$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial (after adding) | 0.300 | $0.400+s$ | 0.100 |
| Change | −0.050 | −0.150 | +0.100 |
| New equilibrium | 0.250 | $0.250+s$ | 0.200 |

$K_{eq}$ is unchanged (constant temperature): $\dfrac{(0.200)^2}{(0.250)(0.250+s)^3}=0.521\Rightarrow(0.250+s)^3=0.307\Rightarrow0.250+s=0.675$

$$s=0.425\ \text{mol of }\text{H}_2\text{ must be added}$$

questions.question: Sulfur trioxide decomposes at temperature $T_1$: $2\text{SO}_3(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{SO}_2(g)+\text{O}_2(g)$, $\Delta H=+196\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The graph shows the concentrations of $\text{SO}_3$ (falling from $0.40$ to $0.10$ mol L$^{-1}$) and of $\text{O}_2$ (rising to $0.15$ mol L$^{-1}$) over 6 minutes at $T_1$. Sketch on the graph how the concentration of sulfur dioxide changes over these 6 minutes at temperature $T_1$.
questions.answer: $\text{SO}_2$ is formed in the same amount as $\text{SO}_3$ is used (2:2), starting at 0, so it rises from 0 to $0.40-0.10=0.30$ mol L$^{-1}$ — twice the rise of $\text{O}_2$ (2:1 ratio) — following the same shape and reaching a constant value at the same time as the other species (about 3 minutes). The curve should be labelled $\text{SO}_2$ (see graph).

questions.question: Calculate $K_{eq}$ for the equilibrium reaction (using the concentrations at equilibrium at $T_1$).
questions.answer:
At equilibrium: $[\text{SO}_3]=0.10$, $[\text{O}_2]=0.15$, $[\text{SO}_2]=0.30$ mol L$^{-1}$.
$$K_{eq}=\frac{[\text{SO}_2]^2[\text{O}_2]}{[\text{SO}_3]^2}=\frac{(0.30)^2(0.15)}{(0.10)^2}=1.4\ \text{mol L}^{-1}\ (1.35)$$
*(Correction: the school's sample answer divides by $[0.10]^3$ and gets 14, but the $\text{SO}_3$ coefficient is 2, so it should be squared.)*

questions.question: The temperature of the mixture was changed to $T_2$ and the mixture left to establish a new equilibrium. In the new equilibrium mixture the concentration of sulfur trioxide was found to be $0.07$ mol L$^{-1}$. Deduce which of $T_1$ and $T_2$ is the higher temperature. Explain your deduction.
questions.answer: $T_2$ is the higher temperature. At $T_1$, $[\text{SO}_3]=0.10$ mol L$^{-1}$; at $T_2$ it is lower ($0.07$), so the equilibrium has shifted to the right (more products). The forward reaction is endothermic ($\Delta H=+196$ kJ mol$^{-1}$), so by Le Chatelier's principle the equilibrium shifts in the endothermic direction, absorbing heat, to oppose an increase in temperature. A shift to the right therefore means the temperature was raised, and $K_{eq}$ is larger at $T_2$.

questions.question: Two chemistry students determined the concentration of hypochlorite ions, $\text{ClO}^-$, in bleach (sodium hypochlorite solution). $25.00$ mL of bleach was diluted to $250.0$ mL; $25.00$ mL of this solution was reacted with excess iodide in acid: $\text{ClO}^-+2\text{I}^-+2\text{H}^+\rightarrow\text{Cl}^-+\text{I}_2+\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The iodine was titrated with $0.100$ mol L$^{-1}$ sodium thiosulfate using starch indicator: $\text{I}_2+2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\rightarrow2\text{I}^-+\text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$. Titre data: titration 1: final 22.35, initial 0.00; titration 2: final 46.00, initial 23.95; titration 3: final 22.15, initial 0.00 (mL). Calculate the volume (mL) of $0.100$ M $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ required to react with the iodine to reach the end point.
questions.answer:
Titres: (1) $22.35$ mL, (2) $46.00-23.95=22.05$ mL, (3) $22.15$ mL. Titres 2 and 3 are concordant (within 0.1 mL), so
$$V=\frac{22.05+22.15}{2}=22.10\ \text{mL}$$
(Averaging all three titres, $22.18$ mL, was also accepted.)

questions.question: Using the average titre of $22.1$ mL from part (a), determine the concentration of hypochlorite ions, $\text{ClO}^-$, present in the (original, undiluted) bleach.
questions.answer:
$n(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-})=0.100\times0.0221=2.21\times10^{-3}$ mol
$n(\text{I}_2)=\tfrac12\times2.21\times10^{-3}=1.105\times10^{-3}$ mol
$n(\text{ClO}^-)=n(\text{I}_2)=1.105\times10^{-3}$ mol in the $25.00$ mL aliquot
$[\text{ClO}^-]$ in the diluted solution $=\dfrac{1.105\times10^{-3}}{0.02500}=0.0442$ mol L$^{-1}$
The bleach was diluted tenfold ($25.00\to250.0$ mL), so
$$[\text{ClO}^-]_{bleach}=0.0442\times10=0.442\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$$
*(The school's sample answer gives $0.4436$ because of a rounding slip in the moles of iodine.)*

questions.question: The $K_a$ values of two salts are given: $\text{NaHCO}_3$, $K_a=4.7\times10^{-11}$; $\text{NaHSO}_4$, $K_a=1.3\times10^{-2}$. When $\text{NaHCO}_3$ dissolves in water the solution is slightly alkaline (pH 8–9); when $\text{NaHSO}_4$ dissolves the solution is strongly acidic (pH 1–2). Use appropriate equations to explain why aqueous solutions of sodium hydrogen carbonate and sodium hydrogen sulfate have such different pH values.
questions.answer:
**$\text{NaHCO}_3$:** the very small $K_a$ ($4.7\times10^{-11}$) means $\text{HCO}_3^-$ is a very weak acid that hardly donates protons. It acts mainly as a base, accepting a proton from water: $\text{HCO}_3^-(aq)+\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\rightleftharpoons\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3(aq)+\text{OH}^-(aq)$. The $\text{OH}^-$ produced makes the solution slightly alkaline.

**$\text{NaHSO}_4$:** the much larger $K_a$ ($1.3\times10^{-2}$) means $\text{HSO}_4^-$ is a relatively strong acid and ionises substantially, donating protons to water: $\text{HSO}_4^-(aq)+\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\rightleftharpoons\text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq)+\text{H}_3\text{O}^+(aq)$. The $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ produced makes the solution strongly acidic.

questions.question: $\text{NaHCO}_3$ can be used to neutralise both acidic spills and basic spills. Provide one reason as to why this is the case.
questions.answer: The hydrogencarbonate ion is amphiprotic: it can accept a proton (acting as a base) to neutralise acid spills, and donate a proton (acting as an acid) to neutralise basic spills.

questions.question: The pH ranges of three indicators are: Congo red 3.0–5.0 (blue to red); methyl orange 3.2–4.4 (red to yellow); phenol red 6.8–8.0 (yellow to red). Which of the indicators could be used to distinguish between solutions of $1\times10^{-5}$ mol L$^{-1}$ sodium hydroxide and $1\times10^{-5}$ mol L$^{-1}$ hydrochloric acid? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
pH of HCl $=-\log(1\times10^{-5})=5$; pOH of NaOH $=5$, so pH $=14-5=9$.
Phenol red changes from yellow to red over pH 6.8–8.0, so it is yellow at pH 5 (HCl) and red at pH 9 (NaOH), distinguishing the two solutions. Congo red (red above pH 5) and methyl orange (yellow above pH 4.4) would have the same colour in both solutions.

questions.question: A solution of hydrochloric acid was titrated with sodium bicarbonate (sodium hydrogencarbonate). Explain which indicator (Congo red, methyl orange, phenol red; ranges above) would work best for determining the endpoint of the titration.
questions.answer: HCl is a strong acid and $\text{HCO}_3^-$ is a weak base. At the endpoint the solution contains NaCl and carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$, from $\text{CO}_2$ dissolving), so the equivalence point is acidic, at about pH 4. Phenol red (6.8–8.0) changes far from this and is unsuitable. Both Congo red (3.0–5.0) and methyl orange (3.2–4.4) change colour around pH 4, but methyl orange has the narrower range, so it gives a sharper colour change at the equivalence point and a more accurate endpoint. **Methyl orange** is best.

questions.question: The amount of iron in an aluminium alloy is determined by dissolving $80.50$ g of alloy in concentrated HCl (converting the iron to $\text{Fe}^{2+}(aq)$), making the solution up to $250.0$ mL, and titrating $20.00$ mL aliquots against $0.0400$ M potassium permanganate: $5\text{Fe}^{2+}+\text{MnO}_4^-+8\text{H}^+\rightarrow5\text{Fe}^{3+}+\text{Mn}^{2+}+4\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Four titrations used $22.03$, $20.25$, $21.97$ and $21.99$ mL. Calculate the average volume of the concordant titres.
questions.answer:
The concordant titres (within 0.1 mL) are $22.03$, $21.97$ and $21.99$ mL (20.25 mL is an outlier):
$$V=\frac{22.03+21.97+21.99}{3}=22.00\ \text{mL}$$

questions.question: Using the average titre of $22.00$ mL, calculate the percentage by mass of iron in the $80.50$ g sample of alloy (20.00 mL aliquots of the 250.0 mL solution). Express your answer to the correct number of significant figures.

Malic acid, $\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{CH(OH)COOH}$, dissociates in TWO stages. The first stage is $\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{CH(OH)COOH}(aq)+\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\rightleftharpoons\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{CH(OH)COO}^-(aq)+\text{H}_3\text{O}^+(aq)$. Write an expression for the first stage dissociation constant, $K_a$.
questions.answer: $$K_a=\frac{[\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{CH(OH)COO}^-][\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]}{[\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{CH(OH)COOH}]}$$

questions.question: Write the equation to show the second stage dissociation of malic acid.
questions.answer: $\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{CH(OH)COO}^-(aq)+\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\rightleftharpoons{}^-\text{OOCCH}_2\text{CH(OH)COO}^-(aq)+\text{H}_3\text{O}^+(aq)$ (the second carboxyl group loses its proton, giving a 2− ion).

questions.question: Apple jam will only thicken if the pH is between 2.7 and 3.3. The pH of the jam is determined by the first stage dissociation of malic acid ($K_a=3.2\times10^{-4}$). If the concentration of malic acid in the jam is $0.0052$ mol L$^{-1}$, determine whether the jam will thicken at this concentration.
questions.answer:
Let $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]=[\text{A}^-]=x$ and $[\text{HA}]\approx0.0052$ (first dissociation only):
$$K_a=\frac{x^2}{0.0052}=3.2\times10^{-4}\Rightarrow x^2=1.66\times10^{-6}\Rightarrow x=1.29\times10^{-3}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$$
$$\text{pH}=-\log(1.29\times10^{-3})=2.9$$
(Solving the quadratic without the approximation gives $x=1.14\times10^{-3}$ M, pH 2.94 — the same conclusion.) A pH of 2.9 lies in the range 2.7–3.3, so the jam will thicken.

questions.question: An organic liquid containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen has a molar mass of $102.13\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$. When a small amount of sodium carbonate powder was added to a sample, bubbles were observed rising. Its $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum is shown (one peak near 180 ppm and four peaks between about 10 and 35 ppm). Based on the information provided, name and provide the possible structural formula for the organic compound.
questions.answer:
Bubbles with sodium carbonate (carbon dioxide gas) show the compound is a carboxylic acid. $M=102.13$ g mol$^{-1}$ corresponds to $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$ ($5\times12.01+10\times1.008+2\times16.00=102.13$). The $^{13}$C spectrum has 5 carbon environments (one at about 180 ppm, the carboxyl carbon, and four alkyl carbons), so the carbons are all different: an unbranched chain.

**Pentanoic acid**, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.

questions.question: Name and provide the structural formulae for isomers of pentanoic acid: provide ONE chain isomer and ONE functional group isomer.
questions.answer:
**Chain isomers** (any one): 3-methylbutanoic acid $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{COOH}$; 2-methylbutanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{COOH}$; 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH}$.

**Functional group isomers** (esters, any one): ethyl propanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$; propyl ethanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$; methyl butanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$.

questions.question: Which isomer type CANNOT be the organic liquid compound? Provide a reason based on the information provided (the compound reacts with sodium carbonate to produce bubbles).
questions.answer: The functional group isomers (the esters) cannot be the compound. Esters do not react with metal carbonates to produce carbon dioxide; only a carboxylic acid does, so the bubbles show the compound must be an acid.

questions.question: Further analysis gave an infrared spectrum (broad absorption from about 2500–3300 cm$^{-1}$ and a strong sharp absorption near 1700 cm$^{-1}$) and the following proton NMR data: 11.96 ppm (1 peak, relative area 1); 2.35 ppm (3 peaks, area 2); 1.62 ppm (5 peaks, area 2); 1.39 ppm (6 peaks, area 2); 0.93 ppm (3 peaks, area 3). Mason claims that there is not enough information to definitively identify the organic liquid compound as it should also be analysed through the mass spectrometer. Based on the spectral data and information provided, identify the compound and assess the validity of Mason's claim by analysing the range of spectral information provided and considering the usefulness of a mass spectrum.
questions.answer:
**Identification: pentanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.**

*Evidence:*
- **Reactivity and molar mass:** bubbles with sodium carbonate indicate a carboxylic acid; $M=102.13$ g mol$^{-1}$ fits $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$.
- **$^{13}$C NMR:** five carbon environments. The peak near 180 ppm is a carbonyl carbon of an acid or ester; no peak in the 50–90 ppm region (the C–O of an ester) supports an acid. The other four peaks (about 10–35 ppm) are alkyl carbons.
- **IR:** the very broad absorption from about 2500 to 3300 cm$^{-1}$ is the O–H of a carboxylic acid, and the strong peak near 1700 cm$^{-1}$ is the C=O; together they confirm –COOH.
- **$^1$H NMR** ($n+1$ rule) shows 5 hydrogen environments in the ratio 1:2:2:2:3: 0.93 ppm triplet (3H) is $\text{CH}_3$ next to a $\text{CH}_2$; 1.39 ppm sextet (2H) is $\text{CH}_2$ next to 5 H; 1.62 ppm quintet (2H) is $\text{CH}_2$ next to 4 H; 2.35 ppm triplet (2H) is $\text{CH}_2$ next to C=O (deshielded) and next to a $\text{CH}_2$; 11.96 ppm single peak (1H) is the acidic O–H proton, with no neighbouring H.
- **Eliminating isomers:** 3-methylbutanoic acid has only 4 carbon environments and 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid only 3, so neither fits the $^{13}$C spectrum. 2-methylbutanoic acid has 5 carbon environments but would show a doublet (the $\text{CH}_3$ next to a carbon with one H) in the $^1$H spectrum, which is not observed (it would also show a different set of splitting patterns). The esters are excluded by the carbonate test.

**Assessment of Mason's claim:** a mass spectrum would give the molecular ion peak (confirming $M=102$) and fragmentation peaks that support the structure (for example loss of $\text{OH}$ and $\text{COOH}$). However, the molar mass is already given, and the combination of chemical test, $^{13}$C NMR, IR and $^1$H NMR identifies the structure unambiguously and distinguishes it from all the isomers. Mason's claim is therefore **not valid**: the mass spectrum would only be confirmatory and is not required.

questions.question: Ramayan wants to make a banana-like ester, pentyl ethanoate. He is provided with stock bottles of ethanol and pent-1-ene. Complete the flow chart (ethanol →X→ A; pent-1-ene →Y→ B; A + B →Z→ C) to show the reagents and conditions required for each step and draw the structural formulae of the main products A, B and C.
questions.answer:
- **X:** oxidation with acidified dichromate (or permanganate), $\text{H}^+/\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$, under reflux. **A = ethanoic acid**, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.
- **Y:** hydration (addition of water) with dilute sulfuric acid as catalyst, $\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{dilute H}_2\text{SO}_4$. **B = pentanol**, drawn by the school as pentan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.
- **Z:** esterification: concentrated sulfuric acid (catalyst) and heating under reflux. **C = pentyl ethanoate**, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

*Note:* by Markovnikov's rule, hydration of pent-1-ene would give pentan-2-ol as the major product (and then pentan-2-yl ethanoate), not pentan-1-ol; the question's intended answer (pentan-1-ol and pentyl ethanoate) is shown above.

questions.question: Processes X and Z are conducted using the same technique (heating under reflux). Provide ONE reason to explain why the same technique is used in processes X and Z.
questions.answer: Heating under reflux is used because the reactants and products (ethanol, ethanal, esters) are volatile and flammable. The vertical condenser condenses the vapours and returns them to the reaction flask, so they are not lost or ignited, allowing the mixture to be heated for a long time (increasing the rate and yield) without losing volatile substances.

questions.question: A student determines the percentage of copper in a brass screw by dissolving it in concentrated nitric acid and making the solution up to $250$ mL. Five standard solutions were prepared by diluting a $0.10$ mol L$^{-1}$ stock solution of copper(II) nitrate. Describe, in detail, how a $0.010$ mol L$^{-1}$ solution should be prepared in a $50$ mL volumetric flask from the $0.10$ mol L$^{-1}$ stock solution.
questions.answer:
$c_1V_1=c_2V_2$: $0.10\times V_1=0.010\times50\Rightarrow V_1=5.0$ mL of stock solution.
Use a pipette (rinsed with the stock solution) to transfer $5.0$ mL of $0.10$ M copper(II) nitrate into a clean $50$ mL volumetric flask (rinsed with distilled water). Add distilled water until the bottom of the meniscus sits on the calibration mark (adding the last few mL dropwise), then stopper the flask and invert it several times to mix thoroughly.

questions.question: The colorimeter was fitted with a suitable filter and set to zero using a reference sample. The absorbance of the five standard solutions was determined and a calibration graph was drawn. Name the substance that should be used to set the colorimeter to zero.
questions.answer: Distilled water (the solvent blank, containing no copper(II) ions).

questions.question: The absorbance of the sample solution was 0.71. The sample solution was then diluted to decrease the concentration by half. The absorbance of this diluted solution was then measured. Provide a reason for why the sample solution must be diluted.
questions.answer: An absorbance of 0.71 is above the highest standard on the calibration graph (about 0.53), so the concentration would have to be extrapolated beyond the calibrated range, which is unreliable. Diluting brings the absorbance within the range of the calibration curve so that the concentration can be read accurately.

questions.question: The mass of the screw was 1.43 g. The absorbance of the diluted solution was 0.34. Calculate the percentage by mass of copper in the screw.
questions.answer:
From the calibration graph, an absorbance of 0.34 corresponds to $[\text{Cu}^{2+}]=0.032$ mol L$^{-1}$.
Undo the dilution (halved): $[\text{Cu}^{2+}]=0.032\times2=0.064$ mol L$^{-1}$ in the $250$ mL solution.
$n(\text{Cu})=0.064\times0.250=0.016$ mol; $m(\text{Cu})=0.016\times63.55=1.02$ g.
$$\%\text{Cu}=\frac{1.02}{1.43}\times100=71\%$$
